headline: 5 workers die after toxic gas exposure at Sitakunda shipyard
summary: Five workers were declared dead after suspected toxic gas leaked inside a ship being dismantled in the Bhatiary area of Sitakunda.
details: Five workers died today after suspected toxic gas exposure inside a ship being dismantled at a shipbreaking yard in Sitakunda’s Bhatiary area.
Firefighters rescued the workers from the vessel, which was anchored adjacent to Ferdous Steel Shipyard, in the morning.
Six people were brought to Chattogram Medical College Hospital, where five were declared dead by doctors and one remains admitted for treatment.
The shipyard manager stated that an LNG carrier was being dismantled and cutting work was nearly complete when the accident occurred.
According to the manager, a safety officer and others entered a section of the vessel where liquid waste was found, leading to the incident.
The Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments (DIFE) and local police are currently working to determine the exact cause of the accident.

headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud takes [[6 for 55 to bowl out Australia]] in Darwin Test
headline: Hasan Mahmud takes 6 for 55 to bowl out Australia in Darwin Test
summary: The pacer's career-best figures help the Tigers bowl out the formidable Australian side for 198 on the opening day.
details: Hasan Mahmud delivered a dream day with the ball, claiming a career-best 6 for 55 to bowl out Australia for 198 on the first day of the Test in Darwin.
Stepping in for the injured Nahid Rana, Hasan used movement and intelligent planning to dismantle the Australian batting lineup at the Marrara Stadium.
His key wickets, including Travis Head and Jake Weatherald, were set up through deliberate planning and consultation with team analysts to use the crease and change bowling sides.
Hasan credited his recent County Championship experience with Kent in England for his confidence in bowling the right lengths in Australian conditions.
The performance marks a significant start to Bangladesh's first Test series in Australia in 23 years, proving the Tigers have more to offer than just express pace.
caption:
6 wickets for 55 runs! Hasan Mahmud just dismantled Australia in Darwin.

Hasan Mahmud delivered a dream day with the ball, claiming a career-best 6 for 55 to bowl out Australia for 198 on the first day of the Test in Darwin.

Stepping in for the injured Nahid Rana, Hasan used movement and intelligent planning to dismantle the Australian batting lineup at the Marrara Stadium.

His key wickets, including Travis Head and Jake Weatherald, were set up through deliberate planning and consultation with team analysts to use the crease and change bowling sides.

Hasan credited his recent County Championship experience with Kent in England for his confidence in bowling the right lengths in Australian conditions.

The performance marks a significant start to Bangladesh's first Test series in Australia in 23 years, proving the Tigers have more to offer than just express pace.
